clue.text: Where numbers wait for their number to come up

definitions.text: Where numbers wait for their number to come up

parts.words: Where numbers wait for their number to come up
parts.note: the 'numbers' are passengers, a crowd, and 'their number' is the route number on the front of the vehicle they are waiting for

explanation.surface: A place where people queue anxiously until their lottery number is drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number to come up' suggests a draw or a summons; here it is the route number shown on an approaching bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside shelter is the covered stop where passengers queue for public transport.

clue.text: How to acquire grit when matched against Victor

definitions.text: How to acquire grit when matched against Victor

parts.words: How to acquire grit when matched against Victor
parts.note: taking a mouthful of earth is the literal way to get grit, and the idiom means to be beaten, as anyone facing a winner is

explanation.surface: How to develop courage when pitted against a champion named Victor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grit' looks like courage; it is the literal dirt of the idiom, which means to fall defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be killed or defeated, falling face down in the dirt, which happens to anyone facing a victor.

clue.text: With the screw tightened ?

parts.note: a mad person is said to have a screw loose, so tightening the screw makes someone more rational

explanation.surface: Describing a mechanism after a screw is tightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a screw loose' is an idiom for being mad; the clue turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more mentally sound is the opposite of having a screw loose.

clue.text: Sound types of horn and fowl

definitions.text: Sound types of horn and fowl

parts.words: Sound types of horn and fowl
parts.note: car horns and factory sirens make a hooting noise, and owls are birds that make that same call

explanation.surface: Kinds of horn instrument and poultry that make a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as 'good' or 'reliable'; it is a verb, as in sounding a horn, and owls are the birds that hoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Car horns and sirens are named for their hoot, and so are owls.

clue.text: In Spain the poet has his place

definitions.text: In Spain the poet has his place

parts.words: In Spain the poet has his place
parts.note: Federico Garcia shares his surname with a town in Murcia, so the Spanish poet has a place named after him in Spain

explanation.surface: A Spanish poet's rightful position in his country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Andalusian poet Federico Garcia shares his surname with a historic town in the Murcia region of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the surname of the Spanish poet and dramatist Federico Garcia and a town in Murcia.

clue.text: Speeds to speed exit

annotationWithheld.why: Speeds to speed exit: EXPEDITES is an anagram of 'speed exit', but no separate word signals the anagram; only 'Speeds' (the definition) could, so one word would do two jobs.

clue.text: Simple Simon's R.A. ?

parts.note: John ... was a Royal Academician painter, and Iona and Peter ... were the great collectors of nursery rhymes such as Simple Simon, so the surname links both

explanation.surface: Asking which Royal Academy painter belongs to the nursery-rhyme character.
explanation.walkthrough: R.A. means Royal Academician; the surname is shared by an 18th-century Cornish painter and the folklorists who edited the Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to a Georgian painter elected to the Royal Academy and to the famous nursery-rhyme editors.

clue.text: Only enjoyed today by those who are more equal than others ?

definitions.text: Only enjoyed today by those who are more equal than others ?

parts.words: Only enjoyed today by those who are more equal than others ?
parts.note: an echo of Orwell's Animal Farm, where some animals are more equal than others: a special advantage held by a favoured few

explanation.surface: Something that only the especially favoured enjoy nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More equal than others' is from Orwell's Animal Farm, a satire on a society whose leaders keep special rights for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A special right or advantage enjoyed by a favoured few is what sets them above their supposed equals.

clue.text: Half one's energy goes into work

indicators.note: 'Half' says that only part of the word energy, three of its six letters, is taken

explanation.surface: Someone puts half their energy into their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes three of the six letters of 'energy', its middle run E-R-G.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the CGS unit of work or energy, so it measures work done.

clue.text: This comes by degrees, according to the label on the tin

indicators.note: 'on' places the label next to the tin, so the label's letters follow

parts.note: a tin is a can
a tab is a small label or tag

explanation.surface: Something arrives gradually, as stated on a tin's label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by degrees' reads as gradually; it means through university degrees. The answer abbreviates Cantabrigiensis, used after Cambridge degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for Cambridge University follows a graduate's degree letters, so it comes with degrees.

clue.text: Rio colourless ?

parts.note: the Spanish river in Andalusia is named for its red-stained water, so its second word means dyed or coloured; the question mark plays 'colour' plus 'less', a nothing

explanation.surface: A river described as having no colour at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rio ___ in Spain gave its name to the mining company; the word means 'red' or 'tinted', and it can be split as TINT (colour) plus O (nothing, 'less').
explanation.definitionFit: It is the second word of the Spanish river name, a word meaning dyed or red, completing the phrase begun by 'Rio'.

clue.text: Being a substitute for furnishing-fabric trimming

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery and curtains
lacing is a decorative trim of lace or braid

explanation.surface: Upholstery cloth and braid edging serving as a stand-in for something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the place of something else is being a substitute for it.

clue.text: Shift to conceal a queen's whereabouts

definitions.text: Shift to conceal a queen's whereabouts

parts.words: Shift to conceal a queen's whereabouts
parts.note: a 'shift' is a dodge or swindle: the street hustler moves cards about so the punter cannot say where the queen lies

explanation.surface: A ruse to keep a monarch's location secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' reads as moving house or a change; it is an old word for a trick. In the street game, three cards are shuffled face down and the mark bets on finding the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The street con (also called 'find the lady') is a sleight-of-hand swindle in which the punter must locate one card among a few.

clue.text: See 12
It's even harder with a duster

definitions.text: It's even harder with a duster

parts.words: It's even harder with a duster
parts.note: a finger joint is hard already, and with a metal duster worn over it, a weapon, the punch is harder still

explanation.surface: A cleaning task becomes even more difficult with a cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duster' suggests a cleaning cloth; here it completes knuckle-duster, the brass weapon worn over the fist.
explanation.definitionFit: The bone of a finger joint is what a brass duster is worn over to make a punch harder.

clue.text: Bring into sheltered water without the ship creating a diplomatic situation

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside: the verb's letters stand around the ship's

parts.note: to embay is to bring a vessel into a bay
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Bringing a vessel into harbour without the ship causing an international incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it is the old sense of 'outside'; 'creating' is a link, and 'situation' means a post or site, not a state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador's official residence is a diplomatic post, a 'situation' in the sense of a position or site.

clue.text: American licensing hours for Naval Occasions

parts.note: bar time is when a licensed bar may serve drinks
US is the abbreviation for the United States, American

explanation.surface: US pub opening times on special days for the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: Naval Occasions (1914) was written by Lewis Ricci under this pen name; the definition stands for its author.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the pen name of the author of the Royal Navy sketches Naval Occasions, so the title points to its writer.

clue.text: " Perilous " one? Not in Keatsian sense

definitions.text: " Perilous " one? Not in Keatsian sense

parts.words: " Perilous " one? Not in Keatsian sense
parts.note: Keats wrote of 'perilous seas' in his nightingale ode; here the danger is not his romantic one but the cowardly sense of a colour, applied to a body of water off China

explanation.surface: Asking about a dangerous sea, though not in the poet Keats's meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's 'magic casements, opening on the foam / Of perilous seas'; the colour also means cowardly, which is no peril at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm of the Pacific between China and Korea is a sea named for a colour.

clue.text: Some people still look picturesque

parts.note: a group of performers posed motionless to represent a scene, as in a living picture

explanation.surface: Some folk remain good-looking enough to paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like 'even now'; it means 'motionless', describing people frozen in a staged scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau vivant is a scene presented by silent, motionless actors, a group arranged as in a painting.

clue.text: Solve one musicianly clue

parts.note: un is French for one
Ravel is the French composer, and a ravel is a tangled thread, as is a clue (clew) in its old sense of a ball of thread

explanation.surface: Work out a single hint with a musical flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clue' here is the old spelling of clew, a ball of thread, so it is also a ravel; the composer makes it 'musicianly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To untangle a mystery is to solve it.

clue.text: " Rats and mice and such small deer "

definitions.text: " Rats and mice and such small deer "

parts.words: " Rats and mice and such small deer "
parts.note: a line from King Lear, where 'deer' keeps its old meaning of any animal, describing small pests

explanation.surface: A quotation listing rodents and other tiny creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgar in King Lear: 'mice and rats and such small deer'; 'deer' is the old word for any beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats and mice are typical pests, the small creatures regarded as a nuisance.

clue.text: Floating tannery ?

parts.note: a 'tannery' here is a place for tanning skin in sunshine, and it floats because it is part of a ship

explanation.surface: A leather works on a barge.
explanation.walkthrough: A tannery cures hides; here the hides being browned are passengers' skins, on the open top level of a cruise ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The open upper level of a ship where passengers sunbathe.

clue.text: Heroine of a No play ?

parts.note: not a Japanese Noh drama but the 1925 musical comedy whose title begins with No, No, and names its heroine

explanation.surface: Asking for the leading lady of a Japanese Noh drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No play' suggests Japanese Noh theatre; it is the musical 'No, No, ___' with the song 'Tea for Two'.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the title character of the 1925 musical comedy whose name begins 'No, No'.

clue.text: City that deserves to succeed

definitions.meaning: an ancient city on the Moselle in western Germany
one who makes a real effort, earning success

explanation.surface: A town that has earned its success.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the German city once called Augusta Treverorum, and also someone who keeps making an effort and so merits success.

clue.text: Red douane wrecked in a fight

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters of these two words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A red customs house destroyed during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges RED DOUANE (a douane is a French customs house).
explanation.definitionFit: The 1708 battle in Flanders where Marlborough beat the French is the fight named.

clue.text: Not so, that book in its jacket

definitions.text: Not so, that book in its jacket

parts.words: Not so, that book in its jacket
parts.note: the idiom 'not so ___' means not bad at all, and a book left in its cover gathers dirt on the shelf

explanation.surface: Disagreeing about a book still in its cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so ___' is a British idiom meaning 'quite good'; the second reading is a book left unread on the shelf, gathering grime.
explanation.definitionFit: A book left unread in its jacket gets grimy, and the word completes the idiom 'not so ___' for fairly good.

clue.text: Right on with the party music

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Approving of the party's music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right on' reads as an exclamation of approval; it splits as R plus ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form whose main theme keeps recurring, a piece of music.

clue.text: Advanced girls in logic ?

parts.note: pre- means before or in advance
misses are young women

explanation.surface: Precocious young women studying reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the place the word belongs: in formal logic, propositions from which a conclusion is drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: In a syllogism the propositions assumed before the conclusion are the logical starting points.

clue.text: Eloquent womaniser : bird bust-up he had on occasion

definitions.text: Eloquent womaniser : bird bust-up he had on occasion

parts.words: Eloquent womaniser : bird bust-up he had on occasion
parts.note: the American writer was a lyrical poet who courted several women, and in his best-known poem a raven perches up on a bust of Pallas

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking ladies' man who sometimes fell out with his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' and 'bust-up' read as a girlfriend and a quarrel; in 'The Raven' the bird sits upon a bust of Pallas above the poet's door.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan, author of The Raven, was an eloquent poet who pursued several women.

clue.text: A dance from South America or the Friendly Isles ?

definitions.text: A dance from South America or the Friendly Isles ?

parts.words: A dance from South America or the Friendly Isles ?
parts.note: the Argentine ballroom dance has a name whose letters rearrange to the Pacific kingdom once known as the Friendly Isles, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Asking whether a dance came from Latin America or the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: The Friendly Isles is Captain Cook's name for Tonga, whose letters can be rearranged to make the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The dance originated in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in South America.

clue.text: I am out of the way back in church with her

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read in the opposite direction
'I am out of' says the letter I goes out of the passageway word

parts.note: an aisle is the passageway down the middle of a church

explanation.surface: Someone says they have left the church path and gone back in with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: AISLE without I is ASLE, which 'back' turns round. 'in church' places the aisle; 'with her' points to a woman's name, as in Lohengrin's bride walking up the aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for any female person, so a girl's name is a fair stand-in for 'her'.

clue.text: Lordly, Saintly London

parts.note: the London district contains Lord's cricket ground and was formerly the parish of St Mary-le-bourne

explanation.surface: A grand, holy capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lordly' points to Lord's, the London home of cricket and the MCC (whose initials begin with the district's name); 'Saintly' to its parish church of St Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: The central London area is home to Lord's cricket ground and named after the church of St Mary by the bourne (stream).
